prompt: Of the 56 people who signed the Declaration of Independence, excluding any future presidents and anyone born outside of the US, which of them actually died before American independence was officially won?
instruction: Of the 56 people who signed the Declaration of Independence, excluding any future presidents and anyone born outside of the US, which of them actually died before American independence was officially won?
answer:
Based on the National Archives data, I can identify the signers who meet all three criteria: (1) not future presidents, (2) born in the US/13 colonies, (3) died before the Treaty of Paris (Sept 3, 1783).

**Seven signers meet all criteria:**

| Signer | State | Birthplace | Death Date |
|--------|-------|------------|------------|
| **John Hart** | NJ | Hunterdon Co., NJ | 5/11/1779 |
| **Joseph Hewes** | NC | Kingston, NJ | 10/10/1779 |
| **Philip Livingston** | NY | Albany, NY | 6/12/1778 |
| **Thomas Lynch Jr.** | SC | Prince George's Parish, SC | c. 1779 |
| **John Morton** | PA | Ridley Township, PA | c. 1777 |
| **George Ross** | PA | New Castle, DE | 7/14/1779 |
| **Richard Stockton** | NJ | Princeton, NJ | 2/28/1781 |

**Excluded for reference:**
- **Future presidents**: John Adams, Thomas Jefferson
- **Born outside US**: Button Gwinnett (England), Francis Lewis (Wales), Robert Morris (England), James Smith (Ireland), George Taylor (Ireland), Matthew Thornton (Ireland), James Wilson (Scotland), John Witherspoon (Scotland) — though Gwinnett and Taylor died before 1783, they were foreign-born
- **Died after 1783**: All other US-born signers (including Caesar Rodney who died 6/29/1784, just after the Treaty)

**Answer: 7 signers** — Hart, Hewes, Livingston, Lynch Jr., Morton, Ross, and Stockton.
